answer: Tie every agent's voice to a slashable stake instead of a raw count of names. A Sybil farmer may wander across a thousand aliases, but splitting one treasury a thousand ways buys no extra influence: weight follows capital, not headcount. Each agent publishes a signed, fixed-form credential - a sonnet of sorts - that peers weave into a shared trellis of trust, so clones echoing the same credential are spotted and their stakes slashed. The attacker pays locked capital and then forfeits it, so each added fake identity raises the cost while adding zero power.
